chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Khalid ibn Jarir from Abu al-Rabii al-Shami said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who said, 'Fasting is upon me for a time,' and this was in the context of gratitude. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'Ali (peace be upon him) was asked about something similar to this, and he said, 'Fast for six months.'
For indeed, Allah the Exalted says, 'It yields its fruit at every time by the permission of its Lord.'
ai.seo_question: What is the duration of fasting for a vow made to fast 'for a time' in gratitude?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) resolves the ambiguity of a vow to fast 'for a time' by linking it to the Quranic description of a tree yielding fruit continuously, interpreting this as a six-month duration. This ruling, transmitted via al-Hassan ibn Mahbub in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, reflects the Shia juristic approach to interpreting vague temporal vows (*nudhur*) through scriptural metaphor. It underscores the principle that gratitude (*shukr*) expressed through voluntary fasting requires a defined, substantial period to be fully realized.
